questions.questionText: It rained heavily all morning, ___ the football match was cancelled.
questions.explanation: The cancellation is the result of the rain, so we use so.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: Raisah wanted a new bicycle, ___ she saved her pocket money for a year.
questions.explanation: The two ideas add up in sequence (wanted it, then saved), so and joins them.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: The box was very heavy, ___ Farah could not lift it on her own.
questions.explanation: Being heavy caused the inability to lift, so so shows the result.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: I wanted to watch the film, ___ I was too tired and fell asleep.
questions.explanation: The idea contrasts (wanted to vs fell asleep), so we use but.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: We stayed at home ___ it was pouring with rain outside.
questions.explanation: The reason for staying home is the rain, so we use because.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: The bus was late, ___ we still arrived at the museum in time for the tour.
questions.explanation: The clause contrasts with expectation (late yet still on time), so but.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: Boil the eggs for ten minutes. ___, plunge them into cold water.
questions.explanation: After that links the two steps in a sequence.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: The children tidied the classroom, ___ their teacher gave them stickers.
questions.explanation: Receiving stickers was the result of tidying, so so.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: Boon forgot his lunchbox, ___ his mother brought it to school for him.
questions.explanation: Mother brought it as a result of him forgetting, so so.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: The path was steep and rocky, ___ the climbers reached the top safely.
questions.explanation: Steep rocky path contrasts with reaching the top safely, so but.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: We had practised for weeks; ___, we were still nervous on concert night.
questions.explanation: However shows contrast between having practised and still feeling nervous.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText: Zak could not open the jar, ___ he asked the shop assistant to help him.
questions.explanation: Asking for help was the result of not opening it; so shows the result.
questions.subtopic: connect sentences into two+ coherent paragraphs; coordinating conjunctions + reference pronouns

questions.questionText:
Nur picked up the crying toddler and gently wiped the child's tears with her handkerchief.
Nur showed that she felt ___ the child.
questions.explanation: Comforting a crying child shows sympathy and care.
questions.subtopic: describe character actions/feelings and explain reasons

questions.questionText:
The little boy crossed his arms, frowned and refused to share his toys.
The boy was feeling ___.
questions.explanation: Crossing arms and refusing to share shows stubbornness.
questions.subtopic: describe character actions/feelings and explain reasons

questions.questionText:
Eisha jumped up and down, clapping loudly when her team won the match.
Eisha was ___.
questions.explanation: Jumping and clapping at a win shows delight.
questions.subtopic: describe character actions/feelings and explain reasons

questions.questionText:
Maya bit her nails and kept glancing at the clock before her turn to speak.
Maya was feeling ___.
questions.explanation: Biting nails and watching the clock show nervousness.
questions.subtopic: describe character actions/feelings and explain reasons

questions.questionText:
When the newcomer tripped and dropped her books, Deepa knelt down to help collect them.
Deepa's action shows she was ___.
questions.explanation: Stooping to help a stranger shows kindness and helpfulness.
questions.subtopic: describe character actions/feelings and explain reasons

questions.questionText:
Even though his own team lost, fair-minded Mohan walked over and congratulated the winners.
Mohan showed ___.
questions.explanation: Congratulating the other side after a loss shows good sportsmanship.
questions.subtopic: describe character actions/feelings and explain reasons

questions.questionText:
Aira hid behind her mother's legs and stared at the floor when the guests spoke to her.
Aira was ___.
questions.explanation: Hiding and staring at the floor shows shyness.
questions.subtopic: describe character actions/feelings and explain reasons

questions.questionText:
After spilling juice on the rug, Yong did not run away. He told his aunt the truth and offered to help clean it.
Yong showed ___.
questions.explanation: Admitting the mistake without being asked shows honesty.
questions.subtopic: describe character actions/feelings and explain reasons

questions.questionText:
Aleesya smiled at the nervous new pupil and showed her where to sit and how to borrow books.
Aleesya wanted to make the new pupil feel ___.
questions.explanation: A warm smile and a helping hand make someone feel welcome.
questions.subtopic: describe character actions/feelings and explain reasons

questions.questionText:
Although he had practised hard and wanted the prize very much, Ken grinned and said his friend truly deserved it.
Ken's words show he was ___.
questions.explanation: Praising a rival's win instead of envying it shows generosity rather than jealousy.
questions.subtopic: describe character actions/feelings and explain reasons
